messages:
Caroline (People Ops): Heads up — spotted an issue on a terminated employee's W-2. It shows a 401(k) loan as a taxable distribution. Need payroll help to determine next steps. Employee: Mei Liu, emp id 48721, termination date 2026-01-15. Looks like loan repayments hit after termination and got coded taxable. @Ben (Payroll) @Anya (Finance) :eyes:
Ben (Payroll): Thanks — on it. Can you drop last4 SSN and the amounts + run IDs where the repayments posted?
Caroline (People Ops): last4 7321. Loan principal $12,500. Repayments posted 2026-02-02 and 2026-02-16 on runs PR-2026-02-02-07 and PR-2026-02-16-03. Term date confirmed 2026-01-15.
Payroll Bot: Journal extract for those runs: ```PR-2026-02-02-07 / PR-2026-02-16-03
DR Payroll Expense 12500
CR Cash 8500
CR Taxable Distribution 4000```
Ben (Payroll): Yep — the $4,000 went to the taxable-distribution account after term. That caused it to show in box 1. We can file a W-2c to remove it from box 1 and treat as distribution, but need to confirm whether the plan administrator already issued a 1099-R (we must not duplicate). @Anya any tax guidance?
Anya (Finance): If Fidelity/plan admin already issued a 1099-R for the distribution, we should not do a W-2c that duplicates income. If they didn't, a W-2c to correct box 1 and an internal correcting journal is appropriate. I'll ask Fidelity to confirm. Also loop in legal for employee communications.
Ben (Payroll): OK — I'll hold the W-2c until we hear back. If we don't get confirmation by EOD Thu 2026-03-05 we'll proceed with W-2c and corrective payroll journal. ETA for W-2c processing is ~7–10 business days after approvals. Creating case PR-CASE-6722 and will attach supporting journals.
Caroline (People Ops): Sounds good. Please cc the employee when contacting Fidelity/plan admin and include plain-language next steps. Also can we estimate withholding impact so we can advise them if they need to amend returns?
Ben (Payroll): Quick ballpark: removing $4,000 from box 1 reduces taxable wages by that amount. Federal withholding ~ $500–$1,000 depending on their rate (roughly $600 at ~15%–25% bracket); state varies. We'll run exact withholding recalcs when we do the W-2c and include a breakdown in PR-CASE-6722.
Anya (Finance): Heard back from Fidelity: "No 1099-R issued — plan admin marks loan default but distributions processed manually; will confirm final paperwork by 2026-03-06."
Ben (Payroll): :thumbsup: Thanks. If Fidelity confirms none issued, we'll proceed with W-2c and post corrective journal entries, then update payroll remittance records for Q1. I'll loop legal on employee messaging and send copy to Caroline. Case PR-CASE-6722 updated.
Caroline (People Ops): Appreciate it. I'll draft the employee note template (plain language + suggested tax steps) once you confirm. Keep me updated here.
